title: Most fitted ASASSN-14ko random-kick paths need more than one solar-star binding-energy scale at a 1e7 solar-mass black hole
abstract: Can stellar oscillations supply the independent period kicks fitted to ASASSN-14ko? We prove that a finite energy store with arbitrary cooling needs at least the largest drop from an earlier maximum of orbital binding energy. We apply this exact bound to 100,000 paths conditioned on eight X-ray suppression times and fourteen optical half-rise times. At the published best-fit kick size of 0.59085 day per orbit, a one-solar-mass, one-solar-radius star around a 1e7 solar-mass black hole needs median capacity 2.19 GM*²/R*, with a central 90 percent interval of 1.44 to 3.28. Only 0.159 percent of conditioned paths fit within one GM*²/R*. At a kick size of 0.4 day, 5.49 percent fit. Cooling cannot supply the energy returned to the orbit. The bound scales exactly as black-hole mass to power 2/3 times stellar radius divided by stellar mass. A bounded stationary reversible store also needs correlated period changes rather than independent kicks over long times. These results constrain the physical assignment of a fitted noise law; they do not exclude all chaotic tides or identify the cause of the stall. The path fractions are conditional on fixed noise parameters and a constant marker lag, not mechanism probabilities or p values. Code, proof, aggregate results, source hashes and a retrieval recipe are included.

display.caption: Minimum stellar mode capacity for timing-conditioned random-kick paths and its mass and radius scaling. The capacity benchmark is explicit and is not a universal stellar stability limit.
